messages:
maya: quick issue: sample-app (node) fires two separate streaming generations when a 429 occurs mid-token-refresh. hit staging twice this morning.

tony: can you paste logs? is the SDK resending the payload or server side spawning a new run?

maya: logs look like client issues a new StartStream immediately after refresh rather than resuming. timestamps ~100ms apart. snippet: 
```
2026-02-12T18:12:01.123Z INFO StartStream req=abcd-1 user=acct-123 model=gpt-4o
2026-02-12T18:12:01.224Z WARN token_refresh acct=acct-123
2026-02-12T18:12:01.330Z INFO StartStream req=abcd-2 user=acct-123 model=gpt-4o
```
so duplicate starts, different stream ids.

anika: which runtime/sdk combo? we had a similar non-streaming duplicate case earlier.

maya: node sdk v1.8.2 with built-in reconnect/retry. python doesn't show it. sample app sets X-Request-ID but no idempotency-key for stream starts.

samir: streaming resume is tricky so SDK avoided idempotency for Start events. but if refresh triggers an unconditional new Start, runtime should dedupe. we can add a short-lived dedupe cache keyed by (acct, model, idempotency-key) to drop obvious replays.

ryan: agree. client-side: add small jitter and use an Idempotency-Key for top-level starts. server-side: a 10s dedupe window seems reasonable to cover GC and network hiccups. 2s was too tight.

tony: for client jitter: base backoff 100-300ms randomized, expo up to ~2s for repeated 429s. sample snippet: 
```js
// jittered retry
const wait = Math.min(2000, 100 * Math.pow(2, attempt)) * (0.5 + Math.random()/2)
await sleep(wait)
```
this will avoid immediate double-start after refresh.

anika: SDK change: default to attaching Idempotency-Key for Start calls, and include resume_token when doing true resume. document difference clearly.

maya: i'll prototype adding Idempotency-Key + jitter to sample-app and run stress test. i can open a draft PR.

samir: runtime behavior: if two StartStream with identical idempotency-key arrive within 10s, respond with 409 or treat second as resume if state exists. keep metrics on dropped vs resumed. reuse existing per-account state cache.

ryan: need to be careful: some UX legitimately starts concurrent streams (e.g., parallel UI). so prefer honoring explicit idempotency-key; when missing, compute hash(payload+user+short-nonce) to detect likely duplicates but avoid false positives.

anika: tests: e2e that forces token refresh mid-stream and asserts single active generation for a given idempotency-key. unit tests around dedupe eviction, race conditions, and resume behavior.

maya: draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/pull/842 (adds idempotency-key + jitter + stress script). early runs show duplicates fall from ~12% to ~1.2% under forced-refresh load.

tony: add repro steps and script to PR so SRE can run in staging. tag devex and eng-runtime.

devx-bot: deploy scheduled: staging cluster-03 at 2026-02-12T20:00Z. link: https://deploys.redwood/cluster-03/1234

samir: action items: (1) Maya: land sample-app patch, (2) Tony/Runtime: prototype 10s dedupe cache + metrics, (3) Anika/SDK: add jitter + default idempotency-key in next minor. I'll create JIRA cards and coordinate rollout.

maya: i'll also update onboarding docs to recommend Idempotency-Key for long-running/stream starts and link SDK migration notes.

ryan: note for docs: clarify resume_token vs idempotency-key: resume_token = server-issued for true resume, idempotency-key = client-provided dedupe key.

anika: ack, will include code snippets and test matrix in SDK PR.

maya: thanks all, i'll post results after a staging run tonight.
